    - Executing the target operation (pytorch_call, which is torch.abs in this case)

    - If test_dtypes is True, it checks that the dtypes and shapes match (via assert_same_type_and_shape)
    - Then it checks the values with a tolerance (rtol, atol) and a tolerance dictionary.

    - helper_shape: requires identical shape via assert_same_type_and_shape (which is called by value_test when test_dtypes is True).
    - value: compares actual values with frozen source values using the listed tolerances.

    - Similarly, the gradient check is only done if 'source_gradient' is in the item. In the provided inputs, none of the items have a 'source_gradient' key. So that branch is not executed.

The value_test already checks the shape (via assert_same_type_and_shape). So the additional shape check in the Test Code is redundant? But it is only done if official_sign is true. In the Test Code, we see that the meta['official_sign'] is false (at the end of the Test Code: "official_sign":false). So that check is skipped.
